_about: AI-assisted: researched and assembled with ChatGPT (OpenAI). See docs/AI_USAGE.md. Drafted 2026-09-26 from linked U.S. Treasury/OFAC releases, Syrian court reporting by SANA, and Arabic Al Jazeera investigation. Historical Assad-era Fourth Division-linked Captagon facilitation only. Treasury sanctions are not criminal convictions. The 2026 Syrian court expressly acquitted Wassim al-Assad on drug trafficking and smuggling counts while convicting him of unrelated war crimes; this outcome controls any criminal drug claim. Maher al-Assad's 2026 conviction was in absentia and for non-drug atrocities. Country associations are historical and coarse, never current positions. Maher's portrait is credited and licensed from its Commons file record; no other unlicensed photos are used. No relationship inferred solely from shared organization or family name.

events.title: Drug charges acquitted; separate war-crimes conviction
events.summary: The Syrian court acquitted Wassim of drug trafficking and smuggling because evidence was insufficient. It separately convicted him of war crimes and crimes against humanity and imposed a death sentence; SANA said the judgment was appealable.

source.claim: The court's 18 August 2026 judgment explicitly acquitted drug counts and convicted unrelated atrocity counts.
